skill: Complete an implication about a real square matrix using the invertible matrix theorem. Infer invertibility or singularity from the premise, then evaluate each of three candidate conclusions and select exactly the true subset.
reasoning_steps: Read the square dimension and premise; infer invertible versus singular.
Translate that status into determinant, rank/pivots, column space, null space, nullity, and homogeneous-solution consequences.
Evaluate each candidate including mismatched numeric dimensions, then report the true subset with the observed checkbox or radio bank.
response_contract: Six complete source cases have three independent checkbox statements; nine complete cases have a radio choice of a subset, plus one incomplete radio case. The canonical example shows Roman statements but lacks answer fields. Preserve complete source banks when replaying, with documented corrections.
difficulty: Moderate, conceptual theorem application to three propositions, without constructing or row-reducing matrices.
invariants: Real square matrix, positive dimension, one premise establishing invertible or singular status.
Three conclusions and explanation of each using the same theorem; no extra computation prerequisites.
Noninvertibility implies rank<n and positive nullity, not a specific nonzero rank/nullity.
Every finite-dimensional null space has a basis, including the empty basis of {0}.
permitted_variations: Change positive square dimension, symbolic n versus concrete dimension, matrix letter, and equivalent premise.
Change whether premise establishes invertible or singular status.
Vary candidate proposition type, polarity, matching or mismatching dimension, order, and qualifying subset; derive keys and explanation together.
Vary radio bank alternatives while preserving source banks at replay; shuffle positions independently of truth.
essential_vs_incidental: Square shape and theorem consequences are essential. A particular premise, letter A, n/3/5/6/7/8, candidate order, true count or surviving label are incidental answer-bearing assignments, not instructional constraints.
lesson_passages: If dim(Null(A))=0 then A has no non-pivot columns ... dim(Col(A))=rank(A)=n.
Since Col(A) is a subspace of R^n and its basis has n linearly independent vectors ... Col(A)=R^n.
